text:
maria_support: FYI - ACME reported a spike of 429s + high latency hitting their dedicated pool after onboarding yesterday. They say it started ~09:15 UTC and is still happening.
carla_customer: @maria_support yes our app saw a ton of 429s. Example request ids: r-9a1b2c, r-9a1b2d. Latency jumps to 800-1200ms before 429. Happening across endpoints (chat + embeddings).
maria_support: I'm escalating to SRE/runtime. Can someone look at tenant rate config for ACME? They moved to Dedicated S1 yesterday.
deploy-bot: Deploy complete: prod/config-mappings v3.14 -> applied to dedicated config-store (id: cfg-7745).
kevin_sre: Looking now. Can you paste a raw 429 response header (from the customer) or we can pull logs?
carla_customer: Here's one response curl output:```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-9a1b2c
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680000000
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "tenant quota exceeded" }
```
maria_support: X-RateLimit-Limit=600 looks low for their bursty workload on Dedicated S1. We expect higher.
alex_runtime: I pulled the quota mapping for tenant acme-tenant-id: `plan: dedicated_s1 -> quota_units: 600, unit_window: seconds` (from config-store). That unit_window looks wrong — S1 should be 6000/minute not 600/second.
kevin_sre: Hmm config-mapper change in v3.14 had a unit conversion patch that treats incoming unit as "per-minute" but writes as seconds in config-store accidentally. Looks like a multiplication/label inversion. I'll attach the mapping diff: `unit_window: 60` was accidentally applied as seconds instead of minutes.
maria_support: So effectively tenant got 600 requests per second cap? Or per minute? Which direction is broken?
alex_runtime: Current stored config reads as `limit: 600, window_seconds: 60` -> interpreted as 600/60s => 10 qps for the tenant. Intended was 6000/60s => 100 qps. So they got 10 qps instead of 100 qps (10x lower).
kevin_sre: That explains the 429s under burst. Also autoscaler: Dedicated pool saw rapid backpressure and downscaled a node due to scoring rules, which amplified 429s (noisy neighbor eviction). Investigating autoscale interaction.
carla_customer: Oof that matches our timeline. Spike around 09:15 when onboarding jobs started. We saw 10 qps effective cap and queued requests. Any immediate mitigation?
kevin_sre: We can patch config-store manually to temporary values. Proposed mitigation: bump acme tenant limit to `6000` with `window_seconds: 60` (so 100 qps) and hold autoscaler from evicting for 30m. Doing this now, will monitor.
alex_runtime: Also reverting the v3.14 mapping change to avoid more tenants being affected. I'll open a rollback PR for the mapper.
maria_support: @sam_sales heads-up for ACME execs — we'll need to explain root cause and timeline.
sam_sales: On it. I'll coordinate a short incident update and blame-free RCA. Please include the repro steps and ETA for permanent fix.
kevin_sre: Repro steps I used:```
# reproduce 429 locally against dedicated pool (use tenant id header)
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-tenant-id" "https://dedicated.us.redwood/api/v1/chat?model=redwood-small" &
  sleep 0.01
done
```
Logs snippet from node (09:16 UTC):```
[09:16:03] request r-9a1b2c tenant=acme-tenant-id qps=0.9 quota_limit=600 window_s=60 remaining=0 -> 429
[09:16:07] autoscale: node-07 demoted due to latency_score=0.82 (evicted noisy neighbor pool=quiet-2)
[09:16:30] request r-9a1b2d tenant=acme-tenant-id queued_by_router -> timeout -> 429
```
kevin_sre: Patch applied at 09:30 UTC (manual set). Monitoring metrics show 429s dropping to baseline by 09:38. Will keep autoscaler hold until 10:00 UTC.
carla_customer: Confirmed our errors dropped after ~09:38. Thank you!
maria_support: Root cause summary for now: config-mapper unit conversion bug in v3.14 wrote tenant quota windows incorrectly resulting in 10x lower effective qps; autoscaler behavior (eviction/downscale) amplified impact. Next steps: revert mapper change, add unit validation on write, and a diagnostic alert when per-tenant qps deviates >4x from plan profile.
alex_runtime: I'll file the PRs: rollback (hotfix) + validation + add a script that scans other dedicated tenants for suspiciously low qps windows.
kevin_sre: I'll create an incident doc and tag for oncall follow-up and postmortem.
sam_sales: I'll draft a customer update and sync with legal if needed.
maria_support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the thread open for any follow-ups from ACME. :white_check_mark:
